messages.subject: Shinyapps.io RODBC connection issues
messages.body_plain:
I'm working with a colleague to connect to a remote SQL Server database from a Shiny application that will be deployed to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.

I have tried connecting from shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, my own AWS Linux instance, my own Windows laptop, and my own Linux laptop, and all connections have failed.

My colleague connected on his first try from a Windows PC. I believe he's using Windows 10, while I'm using Windows 7 - would that offer any obvious differences?

Either way, we still need it to work on Linux for shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.

I've read a bunch of posts here, and also shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> help, and not found success with any of the tips offered.

1. We have the appropriate IP addresses whitelisted <https://groups.google.com/forum/I'm%20working%20with%20a%20colleague%20to%20connect%20to%20a%20remote%20SQL%20Server%20database.%20I've%20read%20a%20bunch%20of%20posts%20here,%20and%20also%20shinyapps.io%20help,%20and%20not%20found%20success%20with%20any%20of%20the%20tips%20offered.%20%201.%20We%20have%20the%20appropriate%20IP%20addresses%20whitelisted,%20and%20after%20having%20trouble%20have%20temporarily%20removed%20the%20firewall%20just%20to%20be%20sure.%202.%20We%20have%20%20%20https://groups.google.com/forum/#!newtopic/shinyapps-users/shinyapps-users/hs4bQHsk9JU>, and after having trouble have temporarily removed the firewall just to be sure, so that's not the problem.
2. We have been using the connection string recommended here <https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/225408367-Connecting-to-databases-using-RODBC-on-shinyapps-io>, obviously replacing uid and pwd with our own, and also tried every known version of FreeTDS.
3. We have read through relevant threads from this group, for example this one <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!newtopic/shinyapps-users/shinyapps-users/hs4bQHsk9JU> and this one <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/shinyapps-users/rodbc%7Csort:relevance/shinyapps-users/qI10hVxctuE/Bx0orL72FQAJ>, and had no luck trying those suggestions.

The error message from the shinyapps logs is the following:

2017-04-01T14:30:26.719242+00:00 shinyapps[168720]:   [RODBC] ERROR: state 08001, code 0, message [unixODBC][FreeTDS][SQL Server]Unable to connect to data source

So what else should we try? Does anyone have an idea of where the point of failure might be? Again it's okay if I can't figure out my local connection - the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> connection is the one that matters.

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Re: Shinyapps.io RODBC connection issues
messages.body_plain:
Kevin,

Based on the error message it looks like a firewall issue. Or possibly the wrong Host or Port, but if you can connect from another machine, my guess is still it's a firewall issue.

-Andy

On Sat, Apr 1, 2017 at 10:58 AM, Kevin Little <kli...@iecodesign.com> wrote:

> I am the colleague.   I have successfully connected to the SQL Server db in our project from a Windows 10 OS (running R 3.3.0 32 bit or R 3.3.2 64 bit and RODBC package 1.3-14) and from a Windows 7 OS (running R 3.3.2 64 bit or R 3.3.3 64 bit and RODBC package 1.3-14).
>
> So, the db exists and RODBC allows communication.
>
>
>
> On Saturday, April 1, 2017 at 11:54:04 AM UTC-5, mason wrote:
> > I'm working with a colleague to connect to a remote SQL Server database from a Shiny application that will be deployed to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.
> >
> > I have tried connecting from shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, my own AWS Linux instance, my own Windows laptop, and my own Linux laptop, and all connections have failed.
> >
> > My colleague connected on his first try from a Windows PC. I believe he's using Windows 10, while I'm using Windows 7 - would that offer any obvious differences?
> >
> > Either way, we still need it to work on Linux for shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.
> >
> > I've read a bunch of posts here, and also shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> help, and not found success with any of the tips offered.
> >
> > 1. We have the appropriate IP addresses whitelisted <https://groups.google.com/forum/I'm%20working%20with%20a%20colleague%20to%20connect%20to%20a%20remote%20SQL%20Server%20database.%20I've%20read%20a%20bunch%20of%20posts%20here,%20and%20also%20shinyapps.io%20help,%20and%20not%20found%20success%20with%20any%20of%20the%20tips%20offered.%20%201.%20We%20have%20the%20appropriate%20IP%20addresses%20whitelisted,%20and%20after%20having%20trouble%20have%20temporarily%20removed%20the%20firewall%20just%20to%20be%20sure.%202.%20We%20have%20%20%20https://groups.google.com/forum/#!newtopic/shinyapps-users/shinyapps-users/hs4bQHsk9JU>, and after having trouble have temporarily removed the firewall just to be sure, so that's not the problem.
> > 2. We have been using the connection string recommended here <https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/225408367-Connecting-to-databases-using-RODBC-on-shinyapps-io>, obviously replacing uid and pwd with our own, and also tried every known version of FreeTDS.
> > 3. We have read through relevant threads from this group, for example this one <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!newtopic/shinyapps-users/shinyapps-users/hs4bQHsk9JU> and this one <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/shinyapps-users/rodbc%7Csort:relevance/shinyapps-users/qI10hVxctuE/Bx0orL72FQAJ>, and had no luck trying those suggestions.
> >
> > The error message from the shinyapps logs is the following:
> >
> > 2017-04-01T14:30:26.719242+00:00 shinyapps[168720]:   [RODBC] ERROR: state 08001, code 0, message [unixODBC][FreeTDS][SQL Server]Unable to connect to data source
> >
> > So what else should we try? Does anyone have an idea of where the point of failure might be? Again it's okay if I can't figure out my local connection - the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> connection is the one that matters.
> >

messages.subject: Re: Shinyapps.io RODBC connection issues
messages.body_plain:
Thanks to RStudio support for pointing out the necessity of including Port=1433 in our connection string in making the connection from shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> to our instance of SQL Server:

dbcon <- odbcDriver("Driver=FreeTDS;TDS_Version=7.0;Server=xx.xx.xxx.xxx; Port=1433; Database=Your_DB;Uid=Your_ID;Pwd=Your_Pwd;")

Port 1433 is the default port SQL Server listens on (check here <https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/database-engine/configure-windows/configure-a-server-to-listen-on-a-specific-tcp-port>)

Part of our confusion is that we can make a connection from Windows without explicit use of the Port number, e.g. from my Windows 10 system in R 3.3.3, this connection string will work, apparently because Windows knows the port already:

dbcon <- odbcDriverConnect('Driver={SQL Server};Server=Server=xx.xx.xxx.xxx;Database=Your_DB;Uid=Your_ID;Pwd=Your_Pwd;')

messages.body_plain:
Hi Sami,

Packrat attempts to determine which packages your code is using by scanning the source code of your app. My guess is that it is incorrectly picking up the string "data.frame" in your code and thinking it's a package name.

Can you paste the lines in your app's source code that contain "data.frame" (without quotes)? If our conjecture is correct then we should be able to identify the line pretty quickly!

Jonathan.

Hi Jonathan, thanks for looking at this. Here is the code in server.r (not very polished). Dont think i use the data.frame function in the code.

library(shiny)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(jsonlite)
library(DT)
library(ggthemes)

stats <- fromJSON("https://api.trello.com/1/boards/<insert board id>/actions?limit=1000&key=<insert key here>&token=<insert token here>", flatten = T)

cards <- fromJSON("https://api.trello.com/1/boards/<insert board id>/cards?limit=1000&key=<insert key here>&token=<insert token here>", flatten = T)

cards <- cards %>%
  select(data_card_id = id, labels) %>%
  unnest(labels) %>%
  select(data_card_id, labels = name)

names(stats) <- stats %>% names %>% gsub("\\.", "_", .)
stats <- left_join(cards, stats)
stats$date <- stats$date %>% ymd_hms

stats_ <- stats[!is.na <http://is.na>(stats$type),]

finish_dates <- stats_ %>% filter(data_listAfter_name == "Klar" | data_list_name == "Klar") %>% mutate(finished = date) %>% select(data_card_id, finished)
start_dates <- stats_ %>%
  filter(data_list_name != "Ideer") %>%
  # filter(type == "updateCard" | type == "createCard") %>%
  group_by(data_card_id) %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  summarise(start_date = first(date))

stats_ <- left_join(stats_, finish_dates)
stats_ <- left_join(stats_, start_dates)

stats_ <- stats_ %>% mutate(duration = (start_date %--% finished) / ddays(1))

for_plot <- stats_ %>%
  filter(!is.na <http://is.na>(duration)) %>%
  arrange(finished) %>%
  group_by(data_card_id, labels) %>%
  summarize(start = last(start_date), end = last(finished), duration =last(duration), card_name = last(data_card_name))

for_plot_uf <- stats_ %>%
  filter(is.na <http://is.na>(duration), data_list_name != "Ideer") %>%
  mutate(finished = now(), duration = (start_date %--% finished) / ddays(1)) %>%
  arrange(finished) %>%
  group_by(data_card_id, labels) %>%
  summarize(start = last(start_date), end = last(finished), duration =last(duration), card_name = last(data_card_name))

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram
shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  plot_data <- reactive({
    for_plot %>% filter(!(start < input$date_range[1] &
                            end < input$date_range[1])) %>%
      gather(key, dates, -data_card_id, -labels, -duration, -card_name) %>%
      filter(labels %in% input$swim_lane)

  })

  plot_data_uf <- reactive({
    for_plot_uf <- for_plot_uf %>% filter(!(start < input$date_range[1] &
                                              end < input$date_range[1])) %>%
      gather(key, dates, -data_card_id, -labels, -duration, -card_name) %>%
      filter(labels %in% input$swim_lane)

    for_plot_uf$dates <- as.POSIXct(for_plot_uf$dates, origin = "1970-01-01")
    for_plot_uf

  })

  output$table <- renderDataTable(plot_data() %>%
                                    group_by(labels) %>%
                                    summarise(mean = mean(duration) %>% round(0)) %>%
                                    arrange(mean) %>%
                                    rename(`swim lanes` = labels, `mean lead time (days)` = mean),
                                  options = list(dom = 't')

  )

  output$table_n <- renderDataTable(plot_data() %>%
                                      group_by(labels) %>%
                                      summarise(finished = n() / 2) %>%
                                      arrange(desc(finished)) %>%
                                      rename(`swim lanes` = labels, `# of finished epics` = finished),
                                    options = list(dom = 't'))

  output$actions <- renderDataTable(stats_ %>% filter(!(date < input$date_range[1]),
                                                      (type == "updateCard" & !is.na <http://is.na>(data_listAfter_name)) |
                                                        (type == "createCard" & is.na <http://is.na>(data_listAfter_name)) |
                                                        (type == "emailCard"& is.na <http://is.na>(data_listAfter_name))) %>%
                                      mutate(data_list_name = ifelse(is.na <http://is.na>(data_list_name),
                                                                     data_listAfter_name,
                                                                     data_list_name)) %>%
                                      select(date,
                                             epic = data_card_name,
                                             swim_lane = labels,
                                             column_now =
                                               data_list_name,
                                             column_previously =
                                               data_listBefore_name) %>%
                                      arrange(desc(date)) %>% unique,
                                    options = list(lengthMenu = c(50,100,250,500), pageLength = 100),
                                    rownames= FALSE)

  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(plot_data(), aes(factor(card_name,
                                   levels = card_name[order(duration, decreasing = T)]),
                            duration,
                            fill = labels)) +
      geom_bar(stat = "identity", position="dodge") +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1)) +
      theme_pander() +
      scale_fill_pander() +
      labs(title = NULL, x = NULL, y = "Lead time in days", fill = "Swim lanes\n")

  })
  output$plot_gantt <- renderPlot({
    df <- plot_data()
    df$dates <- df$dates %>% as.Date
    ggplot(df, aes(dates,
                   factor(card_name,
                          levels = card_name[order(dates)]),
                   colour = labels)) +
      geom_line(size = 6) +
      coord_cartesian(xlim = c(input$date_range[1], input$date_range[2])) +
      theme_pander() +
      scale_fill_pander() +
      labs(title = NULL, x = NULL, y = NULL, color = "Swim lanes\n")

  })
  output$plot_gantt_unfinished <- renderPlot({
    df <- plot_data_uf()
    df$dates <- df$dates %>% as.Date
    ggplot(df, aes(dates,
                   factor(card_name,
                          levels = card_name[order(dates)]),
                   colour = labels)) +
      geom_line(size = 6) +
      coord_cartesian(xlim = c(input$date_range[1], input$date_range[2])) +
      theme_pander() +
      scale_fill_pander() +
      labs(title = NULL,
           x = NULL,
           y = NULL,
           color = "Swim lanes\n")
  })

})

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

 <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/43529332/how-do-i-assign-the-working-directory-for-rmarkdown-knitr-interactive-doc-on-shi#>

I have a fully functional interactive shiny doc using knitr/Rmarkdown (this is saved as a .rmd file).

It incorporates a .png file from the same folder on my Windows 7 machine using readPNG() from the png package.

I make this work by pasting the .png file's full directory path as part of the file's name in the readPNG() function.

However, clearly this won't work when I deploy my app to shinyApps.i b/c shinyApps doe not have access to my local machine.

So How exactly do I approach setting the working directory when I want to publish my app?

I've tried to just remove the directory pathway from my app code, but then it fails to run on my own machine and therefore does not give me the option to deploy at all.

Could someone walk me through how I set up this two file app for shinyApps.io?

My code:

(note: assume both of my files are currently saved in "C:/Users/NAME/documents/Shiny/")

---
title: "TroubleShoot"
output:  html_document
runtime: shiny
---

```{r ,echo=FALSE,eval=TRUE}
library(png)
library(grid)
direct <- "C:/Users/NAME/documents/Shiny/"
img <- readPNG("paste0(direct,"pic.PNG"))
grid.raster(img)
```

Thanks!

messages.subject: Estimate on concurrent users supported on basic plan
messages.subject_clean: Estimate on concurrent users supported on basic plan
messages.body_plain:
I'm looking at the basic plan for my shiny app. According to the metrics chart for my app (currently in free plan), one user can use about 180M RAM, about 0.7 worker process.

1. How do you interpret "0.7 worker process"? Does that mean 1 worker used 70% resource of itself?
2. There are some modeling calculations could take minutes even in local machine. In the extreme condition that all users are using the modeling process, I think I need to assign 1 worker for each connection. My calculation is as follows:

instance size: 8G. I think this is the total for basic plan, I can only have one 8G instance (or 8 x 1G instance), right?
worker memory: near 200M. So 1G instance can have at 3-4 worker, 8G instance can have 24 - 32 worker

That means in the extreme condition the basic plan can have 24 - 32 concurrent users using modeling process.

Is my calculation right?

3. Some users may also just use the less expensive features, which could take 1 - 5 seconds locally depend on data size. In this case we can have more connections in one worker.

Can I make each worker handle more users for simple operations, and start new worker for expensive operations? The worker load factor seemed to be based on connection count, I'm not sure if this will respond to heavy resource usage.

For example, one worker could take 3 users for simple tasks, and it's serving 2 users now. 1 user start to use the modeling process which take a lot of cpu time, then the 3rd incoming user should trigger a new worker, even the connection count is still within the limit of worker.
